title: Deterministic and Programmable Fusion for Scalable Generation of Photonic Graph States
authors: Yan Li, Yunfan Yang, Zenghui Bao, Jize Yang, Luyan Sun, Yipu Song, Yukai Wu, Hongyi Zhang, Luming Duan
abstract: Entanglement in multiphoton graph states is an important resource with various applications, such as measurement-based quantum computing and memory-less quantum repeaters. While some primitive instances have been successfully prepared, scalable generation of large-scale graph states with programmable connections remains an outstanding challenge. Fusion provides a promising "divide-and-conquer" approach by linking smaller resource states into larger, more complex graphs. However, its practical scalability has been limited by the probabilistic nature of conventional fusion protocols, which necessitates extensive hardware overhead and feed-forward resources to achieve deterministic outcomes. Here, we introduce and experimentally demonstrate a deterministic fusion operation with built-in error mitigation, capable of connecting small time-bin-encoded cluster states--originally generated on-demand from a quantum emitter--into larger, reconfigurable photonic graph states of increased sizes. The fusion operation is realized by nondestructively projecting pairs of flying microwave photonic qubits into Bell states using superconducting circuits with in-situ programmability. Crucially, the protocol features active reset and reuse of matter qubits during graph state generation, thereby circumventing the coherence constraints of the quantum emitter and enabling the generation of genuine multipartite entanglement across 13 photonic qubits. Our results establish a scalable framework for photonic graph-state synthesis, paving the way for fault-tolerant measurement-based quantum computation and distributed quantum networks.
summary: This paper presents a novel, deterministic, and programmable method for creating large-scale photonic graph states. By using superconducting circuits to perform controlled fusion operations on time-bin encoded qubits, the authors overcome the probabilistic limitations of previous methods. This work provides a crucial, scalable building block for fault-tolerant measurement-based quantum computation and quantum networking.
main_problem: The primary challenge addressed is the scalable and programmable generation of large-scale photonic graph states, overcoming the limitations imposed by probabilistic fusion protocols.
main_result: The authors demonstrate a deterministic fusion operation using superconducting circuits that successfully generates genuine multipartite entanglement across 13 photonic qubits, establishing a scalable framework for graph state synthesis.
method: They utilize a deterministic fusion protocol based on nondestructively projecting pairs of flying microwave photonic qubits into Bell states via QND parity measurements on a transmon qubit.
model_or_system: The system employs time-bin encoded photonic qubits generated from a single-photon emitter and measured using superconducting circuits containing a transmon qubit acting as a QND detector. The process is made scalable by incorporating active reset and reuse of matter qubits.
key_observables: Fusion fidelity (e.g., $\approx 89.94\%$), stabilizer expectation values, and the entanglement witness ($W_{G_n} < 0$) to certify genuine multipartite entanglement.
important_parameters: The ability to reset matter qubits is crucial for circumventing coherence constraints and enabling repetitive, scalable fusion operations.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the redundantly encoded graph state is local-Clifford equivalent to a standard graph state, allowing the use of stabilizer measurements as a diagnostic tool.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the schematic of the scalable generation process, the pulse sequence for deterministic fusion, and the resulting graph structures (e.g., 2D ring graphs) with associated fidelity and entanglement witness measurements.
paper_structure: The paper details the physical setup, first demonstrating the deterministic fusion of two qubits into a Bell state. It then extends this to programmable fusion to build complex structures like ring graphs, culminating in a scalable protocol for generating large linear graph states.
why_interesting: For AMO/Quantum Optics, this work showcases a highly integrated quantum platform (emitter + superconducting circuits) to perform fundamental quantum operations (deterministic entanglement generation) necessary for building quantum networks.

A single-photon emitter (pink) generates sequential photonic flying qubits to form small cluster states, routed to a quantum non-demolition (QND) parity detector (green) for deterministic fusion (grey bars). In situ frequency tuning of the photonic qubits via a tunable resonator enables programmable fusion between arbitrary qubit pairs, allowing the synthesis of complex graph topologies. The matter qubit in the emitter can be reset between the generation of individual small cluster states, thereby localizing errors within subgraph units (blue vertices, fading gradient).
